public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 806

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/806](https://www.erdosproblems.com/806)
- [ErNe77] Erdős, P. and Newman, D. J., *Bases for sets of integers*. J. Number Theory (1977),
  420-425.
- [ABS09] Alon, Noga and Bukh, Boris and Sudakov, Benny, *Discrete Kakeya-type problems and small
  bases*. Israel J. Math. (2009), 285-301.
-/

@[expose] public section

open Filter
open scoped Pointwise

namespace Erdos806

/--
Let $A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,n\}$ with $\lvert A\rvert \leq n^{1/2}$. Must there exist some
$B\subset\mathbb{Z}$ with $\lvert B\rvert=o(n^{1/2})$ such that $A\subseteq B+B$?

A problem of Erdős and Newman [ErNe77], who proved that there exist $A$ with
$\lvert A\rvert\asymp n^{1/2}$ such that if $A\subseteq B+B$ then
$$\lvert B\rvert \gg \frac{\log\log n}{\log n}n^{1/2}.$$

Resolved by Alon, Bukh, and Sudakov [ABS09], who proved that for any $A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,n\}$
with $\lvert A\rvert \leq n^{1/2}$ there exists some $B$ such that $A\subseteq B+B$ and
$$\lvert B\rvert \ll \frac{\log\log n}{\log n}n^{1/2}.$$

See also [333](https://www.erdosproblems.com/333).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at
  "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos806.lean#L744"]
theorem erdos_806 : answer(True) ↔ ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
    ∀ A : Finset ℕ, A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 n → (A.card : ℝ) ≤ √n →
      ∃ B : Finset ℤ, A.map Nat.castEmbedding ⊆ B + B ∧ (B.card : ℝ) ≤ ε * √n := by
  sorry

/--
Alon, Bukh, and Sudakov [ABS09] proved that for any $A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,n\}$ with
$\lvert A\rvert \leq n^{1/2}$ there exists some $B$ such that $A\subseteq B+B$ and
$\lvert B\rvert \ll \frac{\log\log n}{\log n}n^{1/2}$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_806.variants.alon_bukh_sudakov : ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
    ∀ A : Finset ℕ, A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 n → (A.card : ℝ) ≤ √n →
      ∃ B : Finset ℤ, A.map Nat.castEmbedding ⊆ B + B ∧
        (B.card : ℝ) ≤ C * Real.log (Real.log n) / Real.log n * √n := by
  sorry

/--
Erdős and Newman [ErNe77] proved that there exist $A\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ with
$\lvert A\rvert\asymp n^{1/2}$ such that if $A\subseteq B+B$ then
$\lvert B\rvert \gg \frac{\log\log n}{\log n}n^{1/2}$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_806.variants.erdos_newman : ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
    ∃ A : Finset ℕ, A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 n ∧ c * √n ≤ A.card ∧ (A.card : ℝ) ≤ √n ∧
      ∀ B : Finset ℤ, A.map Nat.castEmbedding ⊆ B + B →
        c * Real.log (Real.log n) / Real.log n * √n ≤ B.card := by
  sorry

end Erdos806

reformulations.difference: The source asks: for A ⊆ {1,…,n} with |A| ≤ n^{1/2}, must there be B ⊂ ℤ with |B| = o(n^{1/2}) and A ⊆ B+B? The Lean makes the o(·) uniform over A: ∀ ε > 0, ∀ᶠ n, ∀ A ⊆ Icc 1 n with |A| ≤ √n, ∃ B : Finset ℤ with A ⊆ B + B and |B| ≤ ε√n. The other natural reading is per sequence: for every choice of sets A_n there are bases B_n with |B_n| = o(√n). Also, the ABS paper phrases the question for sets of size exactly m = √n, while the Lean and the website use |A| ≤ √n.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: (uniform ⇒ per-sequence) For each n, pick a basis of A_n of minimum size. The uniform statement bounds it by ε√n eventually, for every ε > 0, so it is o(√n). (per-sequence ⇒ uniform) Suppose the uniform statement fails for some ε. Then infinitely often there is an admissible A_n with no basis of size ≤ ε√n. Choose such an A_n at those n and ∅ at the others. Any bases B_n then satisfy |B_n| > ε√n infinitely often, so they are not o(√n). I proved this `↔` in Lean as `Review806.uniform_iff_seq` (/workspace/review/equiv1.lean; axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound only). The difference between |A| ≤ √n and |A| = ⌊√n⌋ is immaterial: any A with |A| ≤ √n extends to a superset A* ⊆ {1..n} with |A*| = ⌊√n⌋, and any basis of A* is also a basis of A. B is required to be finite, which |B| = o(√n) needs anyway. `answer(True)` matches the source's 'solved in the affirmative'.

reformulations.difference: The source says: 'there exist A with |A| ≍ n^{1/2} such that if A ⊆ B+B then |B| ≫ (log log n/log n) n^{1/2}'. The Lean fixes the upper constant of ≍ to 1 (c√n ≤ |A| ≤ √n). It uses one constant c > 0 for both the lower bound on |A| and the lower bound on |B|. It asks for such an A for all large n, and quantifies only over finite B ⊂ ℤ.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Lean ⇒ literal: take the constants (c₁, c₂, c₃) = (c, 1, c). Literal ⇒ Lean: suppose c₁√n ≤ |A| ≤ c₂√n and every basis has size ≥ c₃·L(n)·√n, where L(n) = log log n / log n. Cover A by M = ⌈2c₂⌉₊ + 1 subsets, each of size ≤ Nat.sqrt n (possible because Nat.sqrt n ≥ √n/2). If every part had a basis smaller than c₃L√n/M, the union of those bases would be a basis of A smaller than c₃L√n, a contradiction. So some part needs a basis of size ≥ c₃L√n/M. Enlarge that part inside {1..n} to exactly Nat.sqrt n elements; any basis of the larger set is a basis of the part. This gives the Lean statement with c = min(1/2, c₃/M). Restricting to finite B is harmless, because an infinite B satisfies any lower bound on |B|. I proved this `↔` in Lean as `Review806b.newman_iff` (/workspace/review/equiv2.lean; standard axioms only). The Lean statement is also true outright: counting B mod n in ℤ/nℤ, as ABS do, shows that most ⌊√n⌋-subsets need bases of size > c√n·log log n/log n for any c < 4.

review.notes:
No findings. What I checked, per declaration:

(1) `erdos_806`: the statement is `answer(True) ↔` the uniform little-o statement. This matches erdosproblems.com, which records 'PROVED – solved in the affirmative', and ABS, who 'answer their question in the affirmative'. The cited `formal_proof` (plby/lean-proofs @8822f7d, L744) proves exactly the same right-hand side, character for character up to `Real.sqrt` vs `√`. It contains no sorry or axiom declarations. erdosproblems.com and the teorth database record no formal proof (formal_status 'unformalized'). That means they have not recorded one, not that they contradict it, so I filed no status issue.

(2) `variants.alon_bukh_sudakov`: `∃ C, ∀ᶠ n, ∀ A ⊆ [1,n], |A| ≤ √n → ∃ B ⊂ ℤ, A ⊆ B+B ∧ |B| ≤ C·log log n/log n·√n` is exactly the source's ≪ claim, uniform in A. ABS give constant 50 in ℤ/nℤ and a factor-2 transfer to ℤ. 'Eventually' is necessary: at n = 1, 2 the right-hand side is ≤ 0 (Lean has log 0 = 0 and log log 2 < 0). Without a positivity hypothesis C is still forced positive, because A = {1} is admissible.

(3) `variants.erdos_newman`: equivalent to the source's '≍' wording (reformulation above) and true.

Category, answer and status all agree with the source. I also checked in Lean that the ABS variant implies the main right-hand side (consistency), and that A = ∅ is handled.

Limitation: the Erdős–Newman 1977 paper is available only as a scanned PDF (users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1977-05.pdf) that I could not OCR in the sandbox. For it I relied on the erdosproblems.com remark, on ABS's summary, and on my own counting check.
